_meta.what: Per-chapter key-word bank for "Check my map". App (Mind Lab TOPICS in mindmap.html) wording is the master. P4 video wording (eps 1-22: phone mind map in mm/eps.json, the S.mindmap scene in epNb.html, the key-word panel labels in epN/tl.json) is aligned to it. P3 chapters have app terms only.

meansKind.extra: no app equivalent: accept, never hint at it

_meta.partial: true = close but not the same idea; credit it, but do not count it as a full match in the "you got right" lines if a better match exists
_meta.afterD: what the term will mean once step (d) adds "Heat is a form of energy" to the Heat poster
_meta.detect: a phrase, matched on WHOLE WORDS after normalising (see "normalise"). "a && b" = both phrases in the same node, or in the node plus its branch. "unless": skip if any of these is in the same node (or its branch). "inBranch": only test sub-branches of a branch that matches that app branch.
_meta.normalise: lower-case; FIRST arrows ➜ → -> => ➡ ⟶ ⇒ -> " to " (➜ and ➡ are in emoji ranges); then drop emoji (keep ✓ ✗ ≠); "&" -> "and"; other punctuation (= : · + , . ( ) ' etc.) -> space; collapse spaces; simple plural on both sides (-ies -> y; -ses/-xes/-zes/-ches/-shes -> drop "es"; else drop a final s, not ss). Reference: kwbank_selftest.py norm().
_meta.matchOrder: for each pupil node: (1) exact video term / raw (normalised) of this chapter; (2) app keys and keyAliases of the branch the node sits under; (3) the longest alias anywhere in the chapter. Several app terms can share a short alias ("temperature", "volume ✓", "shape ✗"), so the longest / in-branch match wins.
_meta.proposed: heat > "Heat is a form of energy" is NOT on the poster yet (step d). Do not hint at it before the poster has it.

mixups.say: Exam tip: floating does not depend on weight alone. It depends on the material.

lifecycles.title: Life Cycles
lifecycles.idea: Plants and animals go through stages, in order, from the start of life to adult.

app.hint: Add the flowering plant. What stages does it go through?
Add a four-stage life cycle, like the butterfly.
Add a three-stage life cycle, like the grasshopper.
Add the frog. What is its young called?
Add the chicken. What hatches from the egg?

mixups.say: Exam tip: grasshoppers and cockroaches have three stages: egg, nymph, adult. There is no larva or pupa.
Exam tip: some insects have three stages (egg, nymph, adult), with no pupa.
Exam tip: an insect has six legs and three body parts. Other animals can have wings and feelers too.
mixups.note: Only if the pupil made an "Insects" branch.

detect: oil stops air going into the water
oil stops oxygen entering the water
mixups.say: Exam tip: the oil stops the larvae and pupae from taking in air at the water's surface.
Exam tip: many eggs are laid because some are eaten or do not hatch. This way, some survive.
Exam tip: the young get their characteristics from their parents.

magnets.title: Magnets
magnets.idea: A magnet pushes or pulls without touching, and only some materials feel it.

app.hint: What can a magnet do? Add a branch.
Add a branch for the two poles.
What happens when two poles meet? Add a branch.
Which materials does a magnet attract? Add a branch.
How can we make a magnet? Add a branch.

mixups.say: Exam tip: magnets attract magnetic materials like iron and steel. Not all metals are magnetic.
Exam tip: unlike poles attract. Like poles repel.
mixups.note: Whole-word matching is essential: "unlike poles attract" contains "like poles attract".

mixups.say: Exam tip: write it this way round: the iron is attracted to the magnet.
